The article claims a 'Summarize' option appears in Safari's page settings (Aa) menu as a discrete option (or with a ✨ sparkles icon) on supported devices. The article states that tapping Summarize produces 'a short list of bullet points' and that 'a small section labeled "Summary" appears with 3 to 5 bullet points' — this specific UI behavior (a labeled 'Summary' section with bullet points appearing after tapping Summarize) is fabricated; Apple's Reader-view summary shows a few short lines at the top of the page, not a separately labeled section with bullet points.

The article claims users 'may also see a related option to ask a follow-up question about the article — for example, "What's the main argument?" — which Apple Intelligence answers using the page content.' This follow-up Q&A feature inside Safari's article summary is not a verified Apple Intelligence feature.

The 'Summarize' option described inside Safari's Reader/Aa page-settings menu is a fabricated UI element. Apple Intelligence article summarization in Safari is triggered via the share sheet → 'Summarize' action, or via the Reader view's built-in summarize button on the article itself — it is not presented as an option within the Aa page-settings menu itself (no ✨ sparkles icon entry inside that menu).

Step 4 describes a 'Summarize' button appearing on the article itself in Safari Reader view and a 'Summarize' option in the Share sheet — this is a fabricated UI element. Apple Intelligence web article summarization is not a built-in Safari Reader/Share-sheet feature; users access it via the Apple Intelligence website summarization in Safari's address bar, not via a 'Summarize' button on the article or a Share-sheet action.

Step 3 and the 'Common mistakes' section imply that Reader view is required for the summarization feature, which is inaccurate — Apple Intelligence can summarize from the standard page, and the article/Share-sheet 'Summarize' controls as described do not exist.

Step 4 describes a 'Summarize' option appearing in the Safari Reader-mode page menu (the Aa panel) — this UI element does not exist in Safari. Safari's Reader mode has never included a Summarize button in its page settings menu. This is a fabricated UI element.
